title: Request Causal Path Explorer: interactive path & span context panel
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design an interactive Causal Path Explorer panel inside the Redwood Console to help engineers visually trace a single request's causal span graph, correlate logs/metrics, and filter by correlation IDs and attributes.
background: Customers building production LLM apps need to quickly understand request-level failures and latency spikes. Current Console trace views show timelines and raw spans but lack a focused, exploratory workspace for causal relationships (fan-out, retries, async queues) and rapid filter pivoting. This work synthesizes tracing, logs links, and request attributes into a single panel for deep investigation.
goals: Provide a compact 'path-first' view that visualizes causal relationships between spans (parent/child, cross-service fan-outs).
Allow inline span expansion to surface metadata (tags, durations, error details, model variants used).
Offer sticky correlation ID controls and multi-facet filters (status, latency bucket, model, region) that update the path in real time.
Enable quick context jumps: open related logs, metrics charts, linked GitHub PRS or deployments from a span.
Support copyable observability artifacts: prefilled query strings, time windows, and a shareable permalink for postmortems.
non_goals: This design will not replace the full trace timeline workspace — it's a targeted drilldown for single-request causality investigations.
We will not implement a custom trace storage system as part of this ticket; backend will rely on existing trace APIs.
We will not build a general-purpose graph editor; visualization is read-only with predetermined interaction affordances.
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to visually see which downstream calls were triggered by a failing request so I can identify the root cause path.
As an ML platform engineer, I want to filter requests that used a specific model variant and see their causal graphs to validate rollout behavior.
As a support engineer, I want to copy a permalink with time window and correlation ID to share with the team in a ticket.
acceptance_criteria: UI presents a directed acyclic graph (DAG) style visualization with nodes grouped by service/component and edges showing call direction.
Clicking a node opens an inline detail pane with span attributes (start/end time, duration, error, tags, model id, instance id) and links to logs/metrics.
A correlation ID input and saved filter bar updates the visualization and related list of spans within 300ms for typical result sets (UX target).
Users can export a permalink that encodes time window, correlation id, and active filters.
Design passes accessibility checks for keyboard navigation and color contrast; alt text for visuals provided.
design_notes: Prefer a left rail with time range + filter controls, central canvas for path visualization, and right-side flyout for span details to maximize horizontal space for long paths.
Use aggregation for dense fan-outs: collapse groups into 'n children' nodes with expand affordance to avoid overwhelming the canvas.
Incorporate token-cost awareness: when a span represents an LLM call show token estimates and model variant badges.
Provide 'focus mode' to isolate a subtree (contextual zoom) and 'reverse-trace' to show upstream callers.
interactions: Hover node -> show compact tooltip (service, op, duration, status) with brief link to logs.
Click node -> open right flyout with full span metadata and action buttons (Open logs, Open metrics, Open deployment, Copy permalink).
Shift+click nodes -> multi-select for comparative view; toolbar shows aggregated durations and error counts.
Drag canvas to pan; mousewheel or pinch to zoom. Double-click node -> center + expand children.
Filters in top bar are combinatorial (AND by default) with quick toggles for common presets (errors, >500ms, model=redwood-1).
technical_considerations: Backend trace API must provide parent/child relationships and tags for spans returned by correlation ID queries.
Need an edges-first query mode to limit returned nodes within a time window to keep graph sizes bounded.
Consider client-side incremental rendering for large graphs using canvas/WebGL; fallback to SVG for small graphs for crisp accessibility.
Coordination with ENG teams ENG-1842 for trace API pagination and ENG-2201 for model metadata enrichment.
performance_considerations: Cap initial graph to 500 nodes; show 'show more' controls to request further depth to avoid browser OOMs.
Use progressive loading: render root path first, then fetch children lazily on expand to keep initial paint under 250ms on 3G throttled conditions.
Avoid blocking main thread: offload layout calculation to web worker for large graphs.
accessibility_considerations: Keyboard-only users should be able to traverse nodes via arrow keys and open flyout with Enter/Space.
Provide textual summary panel that lists spans in order for screen readers and for quick copying.
Color blind friendly palette and patterns for error highlighting; ensure >4.5:1 contrast for critical labels.

qa_steps: Open Explorer with correlation ID from a known incident and verify nodes render and flyouts show expected attributes.
Apply multiple filters and confirm visualization updates and permalink encodes filters.
Test keyboard traversal and screen reader summary exports.
Simulate large graph (600+ nodes) and validate progressive loading and 'show more' behavior.
